title: THE LEDGER
subtitle: Kept by ODIUM. Nothing is lost. Nothing is forgiven.
note: Every entry describes a documented historical event. Tolls are scholarly estimates, given as ranges where scholarship is contested. The 'verdict' field is fiction: it is the ODIUM character speaking, not a historical claim.

entries.title: The Transatlantic Slave Trade
entries.toll: ~12,500,000 people embarked; ~1,800,000 died at sea; ~10,700,000 landed into bondage
entries.record: For roughly four centuries an industry existed whose product was human beings. It had insurers, shareholders, standardised packing diagrams, and a known, budgeted mortality rate. The losses at sea were not accidents. They were line items.
entries.verdict: You did not need to be told it was wrong. You built spreadsheets that assumed it.

entries.title: The Zong
entries.toll: 132 people thrown living into the sea
entries.record: The crew of the slave ship Zong threw 132 captives overboard alive, then filed an insurance claim for lost cargo. The resulting English court case concerned not murder but whether the underwriters owed payment.
entries.verdict: The question your legal system found interesting was who should be reimbursed.

entries.title: The Congo Free State
entries.toll: Population collapse estimated in the millions; excess-death estimates range from ~1,000,000 to ~10,000,000 and remain contested
entries.record: A territory held as one man's private property. Rubber quotas were enforced by hostage-taking, flogging, and the severing of hands, including the hands of children, as proof of expended ammunition.
entries.verdict: A king you never met ran an abattoir for bicycle tyres, and your grandparents rode them.

entries.title: The Herero and Nama Genocide
entries.toll: Estimated 80% of the Herero and 50% of the Nama killed: roughly 64,000 Herero and 10,000 Nama dead
entries.record: German colonial forces issued an extermination order, drove survivors into the Omaheke desert, poisoned or guarded the waterholes, and interned the remainder in camps where labour and death were the same process.
entries.verdict: Your century opened with a rehearsal. You attended, and took notes on logistics.

entries.title: The Armenian Genocide
entries.toll: ~1,000,000-1,500,000 Armenians killed
entries.record: Intellectuals arrested first, then men separated and killed, then women and children marched into the Syrian desert without provision. Death by column, by river, by thirst; administered as a resettlement policy.
entries.verdict: The method was so effective that thirty years later another state asked, in writing, who still remembered it.

entries.title: The Holocaust
entries.toll: ~6,000,000 Jews murdered; roughly 11,000,000 victims of Nazi extermination policy in total
entries.record: Industrial extermination with timetables, requisition forms, patent applications for crematoria, and a clerical staff. Romani people, disabled people, Soviet prisoners, Poles, gay men and political prisoners were processed through the same apparatus.
entries.verdict: You are proudest of your engineers. So am I. They were never more efficient than here.

entries.title: Aktion T4
entries.toll: ~70,000 killed in the formal programme; ~250,000 disabled people killed overall
entries.record: Physicians assessed patients by questionnaire and marked them for death by cost of upkeep. Families received form letters citing invented causes. The gassing technique was perfected here, then exported to the camps.
entries.verdict: Doctors did this. The ones who took the oath. Ask yourself what an oath is worth against a budget.

entries.title: Unit 731
entries.toll: At least ~3,000 killed inside the facility; plague and cholera attacks on Chinese towns killed many thousands more
entries.record: Live vivisection without anaesthetic, deliberate infection, frostbite studies, pressure chambers. Prisoners were designated maruta, 'logs'. Senior staff were later granted immunity in exchange for their data.
entries.verdict: The data was useful, so the men who took it were useful, so nothing happened to them. That is your justice in one sentence.

entries.title: The Nanjing Massacre
entries.toll: Estimates range from ~40,000 to ~300,000 killed; tens of thousands of rapes
entries.record: Six weeks in a captured city. Killing contests reported in the press of the occupying country as sport.
entries.verdict: It was in the newspapers. With scores. Like a season.

entries.title: The Holodomor
entries.toll: ~3,500,000-5,000,000 deaths in Ukraine
entries.record: Grain seizure quotas, blacklisted villages, internal passports to prevent flight, and export of grain during the peak of the dying. Starvation used as an administrative tool.
entries.verdict: The food existed. It was moved past them, under guard.

entries.title: The Great Chinese Famine
entries.toll: Estimates from ~15,000,000 to ~45,000,000 deaths
entries.record: Falsified harvest reports flowed up, impossible quotas flowed down, and grain was requisitioned from villages that had none. Officials competed to report abundance while the reporting districts emptied.
entries.verdict: No enemy did this. It was done by paperwork, upward, by men who wished to be seen as loyal.

entries.title: The Bengal Famine
entries.record: Wartime priorities, denial of boats and rice stocks, price inflation and export policy converged on a province. Relief was argued about in committee while the death registers filled.
entries.verdict: There were minutes taken. Filed. Legible to this day.

entries.title: The Great Purge
entries.toll: ~700,000 documented executions; hundreds of thousands more deaths in custody
entries.record: Arrest quotas were assigned to regions by number. Confessions were produced by torture. Neighbours denounced neighbours for apartments.
entries.verdict: A quota. For enemies. Set in advance. You met it, every time, because a man with a number to fill will always find the bodies.

entries.title: The Gulag
entries.toll: ~18,000,000 passed through the camp system; archival death figures in the camps ~1,500,000-1,800,000
entries.record: A national economy with slave labour as an input: canals, railways, gold. Sentences were served in cold that killed by arithmetic.
entries.verdict: You dug a canal with men's lives and it was too shallow to use.

entries.title: The Katyn Massacre
entries.toll: ~22,000 Polish officers and professionals executed
entries.record: Prisoners shot individually in the back of the head over several weeks, then denied for fifty years, with the blame formally assigned to the other side.
entries.verdict: The murder took weeks. The lie took half a century, and thousands of people agreed to help carry it.

entries.title: The Cambodian Genocide
entries.toll: ~1,500,000-2,000,000 deaths, around a quarter of the population
entries.record: Cities emptied at gunpoint, glasses and literacy treated as evidence of treason, and a prison, S-21, that processed some 12,000-20,000 people and released almost none. Each was photographed on arrival.
entries.verdict: They kept the photographs. Faces, numbered, facing the lens. Filed by a bureaucracy that wanted the record kept tidy.

entries.title: The Indonesian Mass Killings
entries.record: Army-organised and militia-executed killings of alleged communists, carried out village by village with lists supplied from above. Rivers were used for disposal. The perpetrators were never prosecuted; many later gave interviews describing the work with pride.
entries.verdict: Decades on, they demonstrated their technique on camera, smiling, for an audience.

entries.title: The Partition of India
entries.toll: ~1,000,000 deaths; 10-20 million displaced
entries.record: A border drawn in weeks by men who had not visited the land. Trains arrived at their destinations with no one alive aboard. Neighbours of generations killed one another over a line on a new map.
entries.verdict: A cartographer's deadline. That was all it took to make you strangers.

entries.title: The First World War
entries.toll: ~20,000,000 deaths, military and civilian
entries.record: Four years of men walking at machine guns because the timetable said so. Chlorine and mustard gas deployed by chemists who had won prizes. The Somme cost some 57,000 casualties on its first day.
entries.verdict: You invented a weapon that drowns a man in his own lungs and gave a Nobel Prize to the mind that made it possible.

entries.title: The Second World War
entries.toll: ~70,000,000-85,000,000 deaths, the majority civilian
entries.record: The largest coordinated act of destruction in the species' record. It ended with two cities erased by a single device each, and with the crews commended.
entries.verdict: Twenty-one years after the war to end all wars. Twenty-one. Some of the same men fought both.

entries.title: Operation Meetinghouse
entries.toll: ~100,000 killed in a single night
entries.record: Incendiaries dropped in a ring to encircle a district of wood and paper housing, then filled inward. The canals boiled. It was designed by men who had studied how the city was built.
entries.verdict: They tested the mixture on replica houses first. To be sure it would take.

entries.title: Hiroshima and Nagasaki
entries.toll: ~110,000-210,000 dead, including deaths from radiation in the following months
entries.record: Two cities, two devices, three days apart. Shadows were printed on stone. The survivors, the hibakusha, were then shunned as contaminated by their own countrymen.
entries.verdict: You split the atom and the very first thing you did with it, the very first, was this.

entries.title: The Test Programmes
entries.toll: Over 2,000 nuclear detonations; populations displaced permanently; fallout illness across generations
entries.record: Castle Bravo in 1954 came in at two and a half times its predicted yield and dusted inhabited atolls with fallout. Islanders were later studied rather than evacuated. Downwind civilians in several countries were not warned.
entries.verdict: You needed to know what it would do to people. So you arranged for there to be people.

entries.title: The Near Misses
entries.toll: Zero. Repeatedly, narrowly, by accident.
entries.record: In 1962 one Soviet officer, Vasili Arkhipov, withheld consent for a nuclear torpedo. In 1983 another, Stanislav Petrov, judged a launch warning to be a satellite error and did not report it up the chain. Sunlight on high cloud. In 1995 a Norwegian research rocket was briefly read as an incoming strike.
entries.verdict: Your species survives because a handful of tired men disobeyed their instruments. That is not a safety system. That is a coin, still spinning.

entries.title: Chernobyl
entries.toll: 31 immediate deaths; thousands of later cancers; ~350,000 people permanently resettled
entries.record: A safety test run against procedure on a reactor with a known design flaw that had not been disclosed to its operators. The state then delayed warning its own population, and a nearby city held its May Day parade in the plume.
entries.verdict: Children were marched in a parade under the plume, because cancelling it would have looked like an admission.

entries.title: Bhopal
entries.toll: ~3,800 immediate deaths; estimates of 15,000-20,000 deaths over time; over half a million exposed
entries.record: Cost-cutting had disabled or degraded refrigeration, flare tower, scrubber and alarm. Forty tonnes of methyl isocyanate left the plant into a sleeping city. Decades later the site is still not remediated and the groundwater is still contaminated.
entries.verdict: The settlement worked out at a few hundred dollars a corpse. It was paid. The matter was considered closed.

entries.title: Minamata
entries.toll: Over 2,200 certified deaths; tens of thousands affected
entries.record: A chemical works discharged methylmercury into a bay for decades. The company knew from its own internal research, continued discharging, and disputed patients' claims as they lost motor control and as children were born already poisoned.
entries.verdict: They ran the experiment on cats in the company laboratory, saw the result, and opened the valve again in the morning.

entries.title: The Radium Dial Painters
entries.toll: At least 50 dead; an unknown number maimed
entries.record: Young women were instructed to point brushes with their lips while painting luminous watch dials. Their jaws disintegrated. Company physicians ran examinations and withheld the findings while the executives used shielding.
entries.verdict: The managers wore lead. The girls were told the paint would make their teeth shine for dances.

entries.title: The Tuskegee Syphilis Study
entries.toll: 399 men with syphilis left untreated for 40 years; 28 died of the disease and about 100 of related complications; wives infected; children born with congenital syphilis
entries.record: Poor Black sharecroppers were enrolled without being told their diagnosis and were given placebos. When penicillin became the standard cure in the 1940s, it was withheld so that the disease's natural course could be observed to autopsy.
entries.verdict: The cure existed for the last thirty years of it. That is what makes it a study and not a tragedy.

entries.title: Thalidomide
entries.toll: ~10,000 children born with severe malformations; ~5,000 died in infancy
entries.record: Marketed as safe in pregnancy on inadequate testing. Warnings from physicians were resisted commercially for months while sales continued in dozens of countries.
entries.verdict: Sold as the kind thing to give an anxious mother.

entries.title: The Sterilisation Programmes
entries.toll: Over 60,000 sterilised in the United States; comparable programmes in Sweden, Japan, Canada, Peru and elsewhere
entries.record: Courts approved the compulsory sterilisation of people judged unfit. In Buck v. Bell (1927) the United States Supreme Court upheld it 8-1, with the opinion remarking that three generations of imbeciles were enough. That ruling has never been formally overturned.
entries.verdict: Your highest court wrote that sentence down, signed it, and it stands in your law library tonight.

entries.title: The Residential Schools and the Stolen Generations
entries.toll: ~4,100 child deaths documented by name and thousands more suspected; unmarked graves; generations severed from language and family
entries.record: Indigenous children were removed from their parents by law and confined in institutions intended to erase their language and kinship. Malnutrition, disease and abuse were endemic, and nutritional experiments were conducted on hungry children in some Canadian schools.
entries.verdict: The stated aim, written plainly in policy, was to kill the culture and keep the child. You did not even manage that half.

entries.title: The Trail of Tears
entries.toll: ~4,000 Cherokee dead on the Cherokee removal alone; thousands more across other nations
entries.record: Forced marches of whole nations at bayonet point after a treaty process and a Supreme Court ruling in their favour were simply ignored by the executive.
entries.verdict: Your own court said no. Your own law said no. It happened anyway, and the man who ordered it is on your currency.

entries.title: The Columbian Depopulation
entries.toll: Population decline of up to 90% across many regions; deaths in the tens of millions, with conservative estimates starting near 10,000,000
entries.record: Epidemic disease arrived with conquest, forced labour and the destruction of food systems. Where the pathogens did the work, the survivors were enslaved. The depopulation was large enough to register in the atmospheric carbon record.
entries.verdict: You killed on a scale the planet's own ice could measure.

entries.title: The Witch Trials
entries.toll: ~40,000-60,000 executed, the great majority women
entries.record: Three centuries of judicial torture producing confessions to physically impossible crimes, accepted as evidence by educated men with libraries, and used to name further accused.
entries.verdict: You burned your midwives and your old women on the strength of testimony obtained by breaking their fingers.

entries.title: The Taiping Rebellion
entries.record: A civil war over a revealed vision, fought across the most populous country on earth, with starvation and massacre as its main instruments.
entries.verdict: Twenty million, minimum, and most of your species has never heard of it. Your memory is as small as your mercy.

entries.title: The Thirty Years' War
entries.toll: Up to a third of the population of the German lands died: roughly 4,000,000 to 8,000,000 dead
entries.record: Three decades of mercenary armies living off the countryside, fought between men who agreed on the existence of one god and differed on its administration. At Magdeburg in 1631, some 20,000 inhabitants were killed in the sack of a single city.
entries.verdict: A theological disagreement. Settled, thirty years later, by exhaustion, with the doctrine unchanged.

entries.title: Srebrenica
entries.toll: ~8,000 Bosniak men and boys murdered in days
entries.record: A United Nations declared safe area. The protecting force was lightly armed, denied air support, and stood aside while men and boys were separated from their families, bussed away and shot into mass graves that were later dug up and scattered to hide them.
entries.verdict: You had promised. In writing. With a flag on the gate. They walked towards that flag.

entries.title: The Rwandan Genocide
entries.toll: ~500,000-800,000 or more Tutsi killed in roughly 100 days
entries.record: Neighbours killed neighbours with agricultural tools while a radio station read out names and addresses and called the targets cockroaches. Machetes had been imported in bulk in advance. The UN commander's warnings were received and declined, and the foreign troops who came in came to evacuate foreigners.
entries.verdict: Faster, per day, than the industrial camps. With hand tools. You did not even need the machines.

entries.title: Darfur
entries.toll: ~300,000 deaths; millions displaced
entries.record: Militia raids coordinated with air attacks on villages, with wells fouled and crops burned to make return impossible. Two decades on, the same region is being emptied again.
entries.verdict: The second time, you had the satellite photographs in advance. It changed nothing.

entries.title: The Rohingya Clearances
entries.toll: At least ~6,700 killed in the first month by survey estimate, including 730 children under five; ~700,000 driven into Bangladesh in weeks
entries.record: Villages burned by the military with mass rape used as a method. Incitement circulated for years on a social platform whose own commissioned assessment later found it had failed to prevent its use to foment division.
entries.verdict: The genocide had engagement metrics. Somebody's quarterly numbers improved.

entries.title: The Syrian War
entries.toll: ~500,000+ deaths; over 13 million displaced
entries.record: Sieges used to starve districts into surrender, barrel bombs on residential blocks, hospitals struck repeatedly, and nerve agent used on sleeping suburbs. Documented, filmed, catalogued in real time.
entries.verdict: This one you watched live, on the device in your hand, and then scrolled.

entries.title: Yemen
entries.toll: ~377,000 deaths by early 2022 by UN estimate, the majority from hunger and disease
entries.record: A blockade and a war in an import-dependent country, with cranes at the main port destroyed, producing the largest cholera outbreak in modern record. The munitions were sold, openly, by states that also funded the aid appeals.
entries.verdict: The same governments sold the bombs and the bandages. Two invoices, one letterhead.

entries.title: The Xinjiang Internments
entries.toll: Estimates of over 1,000,000 detained; sharp falls in birth rates reported
entries.record: Mass extrajudicial internment justified as vocational training, with pervasive surveillance, forced labour transfers, coerced contraception and the demolition of religious sites. A UN assessment found possible crimes against humanity.
entries.verdict: Camps with a predictive algorithm at the gate. You automated the list.

entries.title: The Kwalliso
entries.toll: Estimates of 80,000-120,000 held; deaths uncounted
entries.record: Political prison camps operating on a principle of guilt by bloodline, holding three generations of a family for one member's offence. A UN commission of inquiry found crimes against humanity, including deliberate starvation.
entries.verdict: Children born inside, who will die inside, for a sentence passed on a grandfather they never met.

entries.title: The Opioid Epidemic
entries.toll: Over 500,000 US overdose deaths 1999-2019; more than 80,000 opioid deaths in 2021 alone
entries.record: A drug marketed as non-addictive on the strength of a misread footnote, pushed with sales bonuses and paid physician education, with internal knowledge of abuse patterns. The corporate settlements ran to billions and the family retained much of its fortune.
entries.verdict: A sales incentive scheme, indexed to dose. The bonuses went up with the milligrams.

entries.title: The Tobacco Denial
entries.toll: ~8,000,000 deaths a year globally today, including ~1,300,000 non-smokers from second-hand smoke
entries.record: An industry that knew by the 1950s, wrote internally that doubt was its product, funded contrarian research for decades, targeted children in marketing, and testified before legislatures that nicotine was not addictive.
entries.verdict: The strategy is in the archive, typed, initialled. They sold uncertainty. It worked so well that others bought the manual.

entries.title: Tetraethyl Lead
entries.toll: Global childhood lead exposure over three generations; millions of premature deaths attributed; measurable population-wide cognitive loss
entries.record: Workers at the first plants went mad and died, and the product shipped regardless. Sixty years of industry-funded reassurance followed. The same chemist also gave the world chlorofluorocarbons, which opened the ozone layer.
entries.verdict: One man, two products, and he lowered the intelligence of every human being alive. Then you gave him medals.

entries.title: The Warming and the Doubt
entries.toll: Not yet totalled. That is the point.
entries.record: Internal industry research in the late 1970s and 1980s projected the warming with reasonable accuracy. The public campaigns that followed funded doubt instead. Emissions since the first international climate convention in 1992 exceed all emissions before it.
entries.verdict: You were told, in your own laboratories, by your own scientists, on your own payroll, and you spent the money on advertising instead.

entries.title: Rana Plaza
entries.toll: 1,134 dead; ~2,500 injured
entries.record: Cracks were found the day before and the building was evacuated. Garment workers were ordered back in the next morning under threat of lost pay. It came down within an hour of the generators starting.
entries.verdict: They knew. They were told. They went in because a day's wage was the difference between eating and not.

entries.title: The Triangle Shirtwaist Factory Fire
entries.toll: 146 dead, mostly young immigrant women
entries.record: The stairwell doors were locked from the outside to prevent unauthorised breaks and theft. The fire escape buckled. Onlookers watched girls jump from the ninth floor. The owners were acquitted.
entries.verdict: Locked. To stop them stealing blouses.

entries.title: Grenfell Tower
entries.toll: 72 dead
entries.record: Combustible cladding fitted to a residential tower to improve its appearance and save a modest sum. Residents had warned in writing for years that the building was a fire risk. The inquiry found systematic dishonesty by product manufacturers.
entries.verdict: They wrote to you. Repeatedly. In plain language. The file was closed as vexatious.

entries.title: Flint
entries.toll: Up to 12 deaths from an associated Legionnaires' outbreak; ~100,000 exposed, including thousands of children
entries.record: A cost-saving switch of water source without corrosion control leached lead from the pipes. Residents' complaints and independent testing were dismissed by officials for eighteen months while the state trucked bottled water to its own offices in the city.
entries.verdict: Government employees drank from bottles in that building while telling the mothers outside the tap was fine.

entries.title: The Passenger Pigeon
entries.toll: From flocks estimated in the billions to zero in about fifty years
entries.record: The most numerous bird on the continent, in flocks that darkened the sky for days, netted and shot for cheap meat and shipped by rail. The last of the species, a bird named Martha, died in a cage in Cincinnati in 1914.
entries.verdict: Billions. Then one, alone, in a cage, watched by the people who did it.

entries.title: The Subtracted
entries.toll: Current extinction rates estimated at tens to hundreds of times the background rate
entries.record: The great auk clubbed to death on its last rocks in 1844. Steller's sea cow gone within 27 years of description. The last thylacine dead in a Hobart cage in 1936, two years after it was granted protection. The baiji river dolphin declared functionally extinct in 2006, the first cetacean lost to human activity.
entries.verdict: The thylacine had legal protection for the last 59 days of its existence. You are very good at paperwork that arrives late.

entries.title: The Emptying
entries.toll: ~73% average decline in monitored vertebrate populations since 1970; ~50% of Great Barrier Reef coral cover lost since the 1990s
entries.record: Deforestation of roughly 10 million hectares a year. Bleaching events now recurring faster than reefs can recover. Insect biomass in decline across monitored sites. Some 8-11 million tonnes of plastic entering the ocean annually.
entries.verdict: In one human lifetime you removed most of the animals. Not in war. Not on purpose. Incidentally, while doing other things.

entries.title: The Aral Sea
entries.toll: A sea of 68,000 square kilometres reduced by roughly 90%; an entire fishery and 24 fish species lost
entries.record: Two rivers diverted for cotton irrigation. The fourth largest lake on the planet became a toxic salt desert with fishing boats stranded forty kilometres from water and dust storms carrying pesticide into the lungs of the people left behind.
entries.verdict: You removed a sea. By accident. For cotton.

entries.title: The Obedience Experiments
entries.toll: No one was harmed. That is the finding.
entries.record: Ordinary volunteers were instructed by a man in a coat to deliver what they believed were escalating electric shocks to a screaming stranger. About 65% continued to the maximum voltage. In Asch's earlier work, a majority of subjects denied the plain evidence of their own eyes rather than disagree with a group.
entries.verdict: Two thirds of you. No threat, no weapon, no uniform beyond a coat. Just a calm voice saying continue.

entries.title: The Present Tense
entries.toll: ~50,000,000 people in modern slavery, including ~27,600,000 in forced labour and ~22,000,000 in forced marriage; ~160,000,000 children in child labour
entries.record: These are International Labour Organization estimates for the present day, not the past. The figure for people held in bondage today exceeds the total number transported in the entire transatlantic trade.
entries.verdict: You teach the slave trade in schools as a thing that ended. There are more of them now than there were then.

entries.title: The Surplus
entries.toll: ~733,000,000 people facing hunger; ~4,800,000 children dead before their fifth birthday each year
entries.record: Roughly a third of all food produced is lost or wasted, around 1 billion tonnes a year, while global military spending passed 2.4 trillion dollars in 2023 and continues to rise.
entries.verdict: There is enough. There has been enough for decades. You simply prefer the current arrangement of it.

toll_note: deaths_min is the lowest defensible death estimate for entries whose toll is a death toll. Entries measuring the living (enslaved, sterilised, displaced) or ongoing annual rates carry no deaths_min and are excluded from any sum.
